title: Estimated mean for grouped data
summary: Use class midpoints and frequencies to estimate a mean, solve missing-frequency problems and judge the limits of the estimate.
objectives: Find class midpoints and construct frequency products.
Calculate an estimated grouped mean using Σfx/Σf.
Use a grouped-mean equation to find an unknown frequency.

sections.title: Represent each class by its midpoint

blocks.text: Grouped data do not reveal individual observations, so use each class midpoint as a representative value. The midpoint is the average of the lower and upper class boundaries. Multiply it by the class frequency to estimate that class's contribution to the total.

Add every midpoint-frequency product to obtain Σfx, then divide by total frequency Σf. Keep the numerator and denominator visible to reduce transcription errors. Include every class even if its midpoint is zero.

sections.title: Interpret the result as an estimate

blocks.text: The answer is estimated because observations may not actually equal their class midpoints. Narrower classes usually reduce possible approximation error, but only the raw data give the exact mean. For an unknown frequency, place the variable in both Σfx and Σf before solving.

sections.title: Calculate a grouped mean
sections.verification_note: The answer lies between the smallest and largest midpoints.

sections.title: Find a missing frequency

prompt.text: Midpoints 10, 20, 30 have frequencies 3, f, 5 and estimated mean 22.

sections.verification_note: Substitution gives total frequency 10 and weighted total 220.

prompt.text: Midpoints 5 and 15 each have frequency 4. Find the estimated mean.

feedback.text: Equal frequencies balance the estimated mean halfway between 5 and 15.
